summary: cockpit_v4.html assigns --grn:#00ff88 to both .si-state.shipped (L64) and .si-state.live (L67). JS color map (L234) confirms: shipped:'#00ff88' and live:'#00ff88' — identical hex. In the orbital visualization, claim nodes (type:'claim', state:'shipped', e.g. STARSHIP_V3 at L241) and source nodes (type:'source', state:'live', e.g. temple.html/focus.html at L247-248) both render green. SA one-meaning rule violation: --grn serves both COMPLETED_CLAIM (closest to SA-ADMITTED: governance object approved/shipped) and ACTIVE_SOURCE_FILE (closest to SA-OBSERVED: object is live/deployed/running). A viewer scanning the orbital cannot distinguish a shipped claim from a live source file by color alone. E63 established a precedent: in index.html, live-cluster/--green collision was resolved by introducing --teal:#2dd4bf for liveness, reserving --green for emotional-state-happy (and by implication SA-ADMITTED green). E69 applies the same principle to cockpit_v4.html: reassign .si-state.live from --grn to --teal, restoring one-meaning for --grn (shipped/ADMITTED) and creating a dedicated live/liveness token consistent with index.html E63 outcome.
